2 تَعْطِيبٌ , (O, K,) inf. n. of عطّب, (TA,) signifies The brewing (عِلَاج) of beverage, or wine, in order that its odour may become good: (O, K:) so says Aboo-Sa'eed. (O.) The phrase رَحِيق مُعَطَّب occurs in a poem of Lebeed, as some relate it; but as others relate it, it is مُقَطَّب, which means “ mixed: ” (O, TA:) so says Az; and he adds, “ I know not what مُعَطَّب is. ” (TA.) ＝
-A2- Also, in a grape-vine, The appearing of the knots, or gems, in the places whence grow the bunches of grapes. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
